passage: It was a Wednesday, after the last bell, when Binita told me she had not eaten since the morning and that she was afraid to go home some evenings. I'm Tenzin, and I've gone over that afternoon many times. She made me promise to tell no one, and I said okay, because I wanted her to keep trusting me. Then for days I carried it alone, watching her push her lunch away and flinch when a phone rang. I couldn't sleep. In the end I decided that a promise doesn't mean much if she's hurt. I told her first: "I'm going to tell the counsellor, and I'll be with you." She was angry, then she cried. We went together.

qa.q: On which day did Binita tell Tenzin she was afraid to go home?
qa.a: On a Wednesday, after the last bell.

qa.q: Why did Tenzin tell the counsellor even though Binita had asked for secrecy?
qa.a: Tenzin was afraid Binita was in real danger and realised a promise doesn't mean much if she's hurt. Carrying it alone kept Tenzin awake.

qa.q: What did Tenzin do well in how the secret was broken?
qa.a: Tenzin told Binita first what would happen, and offered to go with her, so it did not feel like a betrayal behind her back. 🤍

qa.q: How might Binita have felt when Tenzin said the counsellor would be told?
qa.a: Angry at first, perhaps scared of what would happen, and then she cried, which may show relief that someone was taking her situation seriously.

grounding: The protagonist fears a friend is in danger and tells a trusted adult, telling the friend first, instead of carrying it alone.
